newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan, Spanish firms in joint vehicle venture.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan, Spanish firms in joint vehicle venture.

text.p: Spanish vehicle bodybuilder Irizar and a Moroccan group have signed an agreement to set up a joint company producing bodies for DAF and Nissan vehicles.
Mohamed Kadri, director general of DAF Industries Maroc company, agent for the Dutch firm DAF in Morocco, said the new company Irizar Maghreb would start production next May.
"The aim is that the Moroccan enterprise should be a springboard for the Maghreb and even for Africa," Kadri told Reuters late on Wednesday.
The Spanish group Irizar, part of the Mondragon Corporacion Cooperativa organisation, would own 34 percent of the new firm in the deal worth 275 million pesetas ($2.1 million).
Of this, 210 million pesetas would be devoted to the transfer of technology and expertise with the other 65 million pesetas to specialist equipment.
The Moroccan firm currently produces some 200 vehicle bodies a year through sub-contractors.
"With this partnership, the quality and safety will be able to be assured," Kadri said.
His group also includes the SIAB company which acts as agents for Nissan.
Irizar Maghreb aims to produce 170 vehicle bodies in the first year and boost capacity to 350 by the year 2000.
Established in Casablanca, DAF Industries Maroc has a capital of $1.7 million and employs a staff of more than 100.
